svg.text: From a client write to an applied transaction: append, replicate, commit on a majority, apply

g.text: what is appended is an ENTRY
what is appended is an ENTRY
followers learn the commit next round
followers learn the commit next round
-> a slow peer cannot stall writes
it can corrupt the sliding window
Only the leader may append. A write that lands on a follower is forwarded to the leader first.
ServerIsNotTheLeaderException carries the leader address; LeaderCommandForwarder replays the command there
The SQL never crosses the wire. The transaction is encoded as a typed Raft log entry.
RaftLogEntryCodec encodes one of 8 types; the type byte is the whole version contract, so decoders must stay in step
Each message carries the position the entry must follow, so a follower can refuse a log that does not line up.
AppendEntries(term, prevLogIndex, prevLogTerm, entries[], leaderCommit) - a mismatch is rejected and retried further back
The entry commits as soon as a majority has written it to disk. The third node is not waited for.
arcadedb.ha.quorum = majority (2 of 3) or all; quorum=all trades availability for every peer having the entry
Committed is not enough: the entry is decoded and applied to the database before the client hears anything.
ArcadeStateMachine.applyTransaction decodes the TX_ENTRY and applies it - the state machine IS the ArcadeDB database
The commit position rides along on the following AppendEntries, so followers apply one round trip later.
leaderCommit is piggybacked on the next AppendEntries - which is why a follower read can lag a leader read
The leader keeps a next-index per follower: on a mismatch it walks back and resends until the logs agree.
a peer too far behind for the retained log is handed the database instead, as an INSTALL_DATABASE_ENTRY
Under load the entries are grouped rather than sent one by one, and oversized ones are refused up front.
RaftGroupCommitter batches up to 500 entries per dispatch; an entry over raft.grpc.message.size.max is rejected synchronously
